overview: Same amplification chemistry underneath, but one only tells you if a target is present, and the other tells you how much.
genZNote: One tells you yes or no. One tells you how much.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Amplifies a target DNA sequence exponentially, with the product detected only after amplification is complete, typically by gel electrophoresis.
aspects.valueB: Amplifies and detects a target DNA sequence simultaneously in real time, using fluorescent probes or dyes read every cycle.

aspects.label: Detection Timing
aspects.valueA: End-point detection — result is read only after the reaction has finished.
aspects.valueB: Real-time detection — fluorescence is measured during every amplification cycle.

aspects.label: Quantification Capability
aspects.valueA: Qualitative or, at best, roughly semi-quantitative.
aspects.valueB: Truly quantitative — a cycle threshold (Ct) value correlates with starting template amount via a standard curve.

aspects.label: Detection Chemistry
aspects.valueA: Ethidium bromide or similar intercalating dye visualized on an agarose gel post-run.
aspects.valueB: Intercalating dyes (e.g. SYBR Green) or sequence-specific fluorescent probes (e.g. TaqMan) monitored continuously.

aspects.label: Contamination Risk
aspects.valueA: Higher — requires opening tubes post-amplification for gel loading, risking amplicon carryover.
aspects.valueB: Lower — closed-tube detection throughout, minimizing amplicon contamination risk.

aspects.label: Turnaround and Throughput
aspects.valueA: Requires an additional post-PCR gel run and imaging step, adding time.
aspects.valueB: Faster overall workflow with no post-run gel step, and better suited to high-throughput automated platforms.

aspects.label: Typical Applications
aspects.valueA: Basic presence/absence screening, cloning verification, teaching labs.
aspects.valueB: Clinical viral load monitoring, gene expression studies, pathogen quantification.
